title: ArcCivs proposed university, smeltery and crusher industry economy assessment
assumptions: Design values approved for implementation; source/package checks and active runtime remain separate. Low/base/high use 1/4/6 participating city owners, 0.25/1/4 active hours per day, and 2/8/24 successful batches for regular recipes versus 4/16/48 for Crusher recipes. These are supplied activity assumptions, not measured cadence. They imply 8/8/6 regular batches per active hour and 16/16/12 Crusher batches per active hour. Each industry building has one worker; each recipe row is one selected recipe for that worker, and alternatives must not be summed as if one worker ran every recipe simultaneously. A 60-second work interval is only a floor before walking and sleeping; supplied behavior says hunger may double the effective cycle. No offline catch-up or skill-speed bonus is assumed.

The package is University + Smeltery + Crusher + the existing Auto Blacksmith target: 11 to 15 ordinary Auto buildings, leaving one of 16 building slots for the Plan Board. Infrastructure 96, population 12 per city and NPC 48 remain unchanged. Four industry workers per city are 24 workers at six high-scenario owners, before accounting for all other existing NPC use; they cannot be added on top of the 12-person city or 48-NPC backend limits.

Auto mode uses separate closed city-stock units and has no conversion into native physical items. Each of seven new products (RAW_IRON, CHARCOAL, GRAVEL, SAND, GLASS, IRON_INGOT, IRON_TOOL_KIT) has a 64-unit on-hand cap. Calculator rows show gross committed item input/output batches, not ending stocks; only committed downstream recipe consumption can free room under the cap, and there is no native withdrawal API. A full output or missing input rejects the batch atomically without debit or output. The assessment does not assume same-day recipe chaining or price these closed stocks.

Native mode uses physical item inputs and outputs; no native conversion is applied to Auto stock. Existing forge recipes stay unchanged; only Engineering-gated BUCKET (3 IRON_INGOT -> 1) and SHEARS (2 IRON_INGOT -> 1) are added here. The Auto toolkit recipe's shorthand IRON is read as the listed IRON_INGOT unit. The Auto quarry ORE output is read as the listed closed RAW_IRON unit. Parent confirmed both identifier mappings.

Research is one funding event per city per project, charged before work and never reset by rebuilding. Auto research consumes closed W/S/F and product stock; native research consumes physical items. These are alternative funding modes and are not added together. The one-time resource totals are in the companion Markdown; they are not multiplied by seven or treated as recurring daily flows. Twenty-one real 60-second sessions total across the four projects; no offline catch-up. If one researcher performs them sequentially, the nominal minimum is 21 active minutes, before travel/sleep/hunger.

Auto L1 building prices are internal raw stock (University 48 WOOD/32 STONE/8 FOOD; Smeltery 32/24/0; Crusher 24/24/0; Blacksmith 32/24/0). Target levels 2 and 3 use the existing squared target-level multiplier; this assessment charges each target level once when purchased. Curated University, Smeltery and Crusher schematic files exist for 3 styles × L1-L3 (27 files/9 families), but the curation report and manifest contain volume/size and heart metadata rather than material palette counts. Their maximum volume is 31,104 cells, an upper bound that includes clearing/air and marker cells, not a solid-block count or construction cost; no native construction cost or money conversion is asserted.

Direct ArcCivs Vault, tokens and player XP remain 0 before/after. One completed resident job session adds 1 existing internal resident job-XP, capped at 40 per worker; the calculator's resident_job_xp row is a one-worker selected-recipe sensitivity, not player XP or money. Research sessions contribute 21 one-time internal job-XP across all projects if all sessions are credited; no cash value is assigned.

The calculator's participants are active owner cities; network-week arithmetic is gross per-owner daily item amount times participants times seven. Resource/item rows are separate units and must not be added to Vault/tokens/XP or across alternative recipes. `disposable_per_player_day` stays zero because net stock after committed downstream consumption is not established; no native withdrawal API is assumed. This does not mean gross item flows are zero. No `prices` are entered because neither current SELL nor contract terms are assumed to be a fixed quote for these proposed outputs.

Fresh read-only 168-hour ledger artifact (2026-10-18T14:16:43Z to 2026-10-25T14:16:43Z): 2,728 records, 33,058 operations, 23 players. Currency coverage is split: Vault has 495 unclassified operations and 20,443,625.26 absolute Vault amount, with 31.8372% classified-amount coverage; tokens have 2 unclassified operations and 12 tokens absolute amount, with 88.3495% classified-amount coverage. These currency amounts are separate and are not summed. This aggregate is not a normal-player income baseline. Requested-material shop selection found only COBBLESTONE, GLASS, GRAVEL, OAK_LOG and SAND rows; missing materials mean no observation, not zero sale price.

EconomyShopGUI SELL and AutoSellChests remain current; planned SELL-off is a separate future state. Native glass, gravel and sand have recent shop-sales observations, but historical effective averages are not current quotes. Raw iron and iron ingot may also match active ARC contracts, whose dated inventory lists base rates and a shared weekly cap, without a fresh active-offer/budget verification. No item is assumed sold through both routes, no new industry Vault mint is forecast, and SELL-off does not automatically imply contract demand. Auto closed stock cannot enter native SELL/contracts under the no-native-conversion rule.

The existing quarry L1/L2/L3 yields are three separate baseline alternatives, each evaluated across all supplied activity cases [2,8,24] trips per owner-day. New Auto quarry output is one closed RAW_IRON/ORE unit per real cycle instead of the old stone payout, never both.

Automatic progression after Engineering intentionally opens existing Town Hall L3 (population reachability8to12), but no automatic old-producer/warehouse/house/builder/BlacksmithL3 upgrade goals. OnlynewUniversity/Smeltery/CrusherL3 areautomatic. Existingcaps16buildings/96infrastructure/12population/48activeNPC andallpertypeyields/costsremain unchanged; fouradditionaladmissionscost48FOODonce, atmost40FOOD/hour addedfeedingatfullwork underexistingrules.
